waiting.title: Performance: start the work in the measured order?
waiting.what: You agreed to measure first. Measured on 26 November (decisions 377 and 378): 17 of the 1,223 functions take 55% of the check's 7.7 hours. The time is in the solver's steps on the whole model. The solver's shortcut of 20 November, the working set, does not help in three cases: where a model rolls, its set is nearly the whole model (two thirds of the measured time); the check turns every control back in one long call, which never uses the set; and a car on the ground or on tracks is left out by rule. Half of the measured time is loop closing, which works out the free motions afresh in every round; Gemini's second analysis, made with the code, pointed there and my counts confirm it. In the viewer the 8110's wheel runs at 0.3 frames a second for the same reasons. Two other costs are separate: the collision test loops over every pair of parts (half of a frame on the 42043), and the two largest models draw one mesh per part and cannot hold 60 frames a second even at rest.
waiting.effect: The proposed order: (1) long turns on the working set, and no second try of the set after a turn on play, (2) loop closing that keeps its free motions over rounds while the gaps halve, (3) the working set where the frame moves and the rules that leave functions out, (4) the collision test with a search structure and the same answers, (5) one mesh per body in the viewer, (6) a check that skips sets whose reading did not change, (7) pushes on a working set. The solver owner takes 1, 2, 3 and 7; the worker 4, then 5. My estimate, not a measurement: steps 1 to 4 make the check 3 to 6 times shorter and bring the largest models from under one frame a second to several. The set work stays paused meanwhile.
